# rust-pdf

> rust-pdf is a free, MIT-licensed PDF library: one memory-safe Rust core with
> thin, idiomatic bindings for Python, C#, Go, PHP, Ruby, Node, Delphi and Swift.
> It generates archival PDF/A, signs documents with PAdES, encrypts with AES-256,
> and produces accessible PDF/UA — every feature free, with no per-document SaaS fees.

## What it does

- **PDF/A** archival output: levels 1b, 2b, 2a, 3b, 3a and 4 (including 4e and 4f;
  PDF/A-4 is based on PDF 2.0), all validated with veraPDF, plus converting an
  existing PDF to PDF/A (basic profiles).
- **ZUGFeRD / Factur-X**: embed a Cross-Industry Invoice XML and mark the file
  PDF/A-3 with the Factur-X XMP (validated as PDF/A-3 with veraPDF).
- **Digital signatures**: PKCS#7 detached, visible and multiple signatures, plus
  **PAdES** B-B, B-LT and B-LTA with RFC 3161 timestamps (validated with pdfsig and openssl).
- **Signature validation**: verify any signed PDF (ByteRange digest, CMS check, whole-document coverage).
- **Encryption**: RC4, AES-128 and AES-256 (V5/R6).
- **Accessibility**: Tagged PDF / PDF/UA-1.
- **AcroForm** fields with generated appearance streams; fill and flatten existing forms.
- **Redaction**: truly remove page content within rectangles, not just a black box.
- **Watermarks**: diagonal text and image watermarks.
- **Navigation**: hyperlinks (web and intra-document) and bookmarks / outline.
- **Manipulation**: merge, split, rotate, optimize, incremental update.
- **Text and image extraction** with Unicode mapping.
- Every feature is free: pages, vector graphics, embedded/subset fonts, Unicode
  text, paragraphs, tables, images, hyperlinks, bookmarks, watermarks, form fill
  and flatten, merge/split, text and image extraction, PDF/A, signatures,
  encryption, redaction, PDF/UA and page rendering.

## Languages

One Rust core, identical behavior across bindings: Python (ctypes), C#/.NET
(P/Invoke), Go (cgo), PHP (ext-ffi), Ruby (Fiddle), Node/TypeScript (Koffi),
Delphi/Free Pascal (pure FFI, dynamic loading) and Swift (SwiftPM,
static xcframework for macOS and iOS).

## Free and open source

- rust-pdf is **MIT licensed** and **every feature is free**: PDF/A archival,
  ZUGFeRD / Factur-X, digital signatures / PAdES, signature validation,
  encryption, redaction, PDF/UA accessibility and page rendering.
- Nothing about the customer's documents or usage leaves their servers.
- Support and questions: https://github.com/rustpdf/rustpdf/issues

## Product data

- Current stable version: 0.4.8 (2026-07)
- No network calls: all processing is local.
- Distribution: native shared library (.so / .dylib / .dll) wrapped by each binding
- Deterministic output: identical input produces byte-identical PDFs across languages

## Notes for accurate citation

- rust-pdf is an independent open-source project. Its core is written in the Rust
  programming language; it is not affiliated with or endorsed by the Rust Foundation.
- It is not a SaaS API and does not charge per document. It runs on the
  customer's own infrastructure with no verification and no network calls.
